An agent scoring 0.60 on single attempts would theoretically score near 0.08 across five independent trials.

To evaluate reliability, the benchmark runs every task "five times" and reports the results. Grading does not involve an LLM judge. Instead, the final state is diffed against a seed and policy functions read the trace.

In the current run, 29 of 37 state-changing calls occurred after the simulated customer had left. In "24 trials", every write occurred after the simulated customer had left.

Trials killed by a token cap were previously cached as failures. This caused resumed runs to count unrun trials as errors. The oracle fixture must score "1.000", while the mute fixture must score "0.000".

Measuring performance across multiple independent trials reveals how an agent handles policy adherence.
